Especially the ice caves. I'm sure they're filled with crystal-clear ice, glittering like gemstones. And the ceiling must be lined with huge icicles, hanging down like frozen spears. It must be such a breathtaking sight! If you ever go there, would you tell me what it was like? If anything stands out, something truly magical, please promise you'll share it with me!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_06: Adventurer... the skeletons were nothing like I imagined. I thought I would feel sorry for them, but I didn’t. They were terrifying. I only saw them from afar, but I was so scared I couldn’t even move. And the ones in Frost Mountain were even worse. Their bones were all frozen blue, like they had been trapped in ice for ages. It was awful. Please, adventurer, can you take care of them? I don’t think I’ll be able to sleep until they're gone.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_07: The Frost Mountain adventure was a complete disaster. I barely made it out alive, and only thanks to the companions who were with me. I lost all my gear too... the ones you worked so hard to find for me. I'm such a fool... You don’t have to say anything to comfort me. My uncle was right. Maybe someone like me just isn’t meant to be an adventurer... What? You want to help me get new equipment again? No, please, don’t trouble yourself because of me. Adventurer? Adventurer, wait!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_08: This time, I don't want to be a burden to anyone, so I'm looking for a place I can explore on my own. I heard the Goblin Caves aren't too difficult for a beginner adventurer. What do you think? Still, the thought of going alone is a bit scary... If you don’t mind, could you check the caves out first? Just to see if there are any safe spots or places to hide, even just a little. Hehe... thank you.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Squire_Greeting_09: Well... I did make it as far as the cave entrance, but... there were a lot more goblins than I expected. With that many, I don't think I could handle even one on my own. And if they surround me, I’d be in real trouble. Adventurer, would you be willing to take care of some of the goblins for me? I think I’d find the courage to try again if I knew it was a little safer.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_01: You haven’t lost your touch, it seems. But don’t think we’re done yet. This is only the beginning of something bigger, something far more intricate. We’ll move on to the next phase soon enough. When you’re ready, come back and we’ll continue this work.

Hmm, this fabric is thick and coarse. It wouldn’t be suitable for proper clothing as it is. I’d need a heavy needle and thick thread just to sew it. Still, the fact that it’s waterproof is quite appealing. I’ll need to give some thought to how I can make use of this tar.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_02: So it was those things that are neither dead nor alive. Where do these cursed creatures even come from? I have also heard of people returning from their expeditions in a rather peculiar state. I cannot help but wonder if there is a connection. This is something I must look into.
Well done. It couldn’t have been easy to keep it in such good condition. Thanks to you, I’ll be able to run a few tests with it. I’ll be counting on you again next time.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_03: So it was no ordinary place after all. The clues are certainly there, but this curse is far more complicated than I expected. The Barbican was no simple defensive structure. The deeper we dig, the more tangled the truth becomes. We may need to seek advice from someone with more experience in these matters.

This liquid is truly fascinating. It gives off a soft glow during the day and shines even brighter at night. Even the way it feels on my fingertips is something special. I’ll probably lose sleep for days just thinking about how and where to use it. Thank you so much!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_04: Good work, but you look like you’ve had your share of the wilds. This curse—it’s not just an accident of nature. There’s something behind it, something that keeps tightening the noose around us.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_05: Better, much better. You’re not quite the mess you were, but we’re far from done. Now, back to the task at hand. I need to have a word with someone. Meet me here later when you’re ready to continue.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_06: Ah, with these materials, I can work wonders. Let me weave my magic. There, now you look like someone I wouldn't mind being seen with.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_07: The bitter cold of Frost Mountain invokes memories of a time when my survival seemed uncertain. Yet here I stand, fabulous as ever! Now, onto matters of utmost importance - securing my status at the upcoming elite soirée. Be on your way so I can focus on what I am going to wear.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_08: Exemplary as always! I've worked hard to reach where I am, and I refuse to rely on any more handouts from my adopted family. So, lend your strength to make these lands safer, ensuring the wealthy continue investing here.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_09: Kudos acquiring the materials. You won't be the one making the offering, for they will know you are an imposter. I have someone in mind whom I will disguise as a potential Dark Follower to carry out this delicate task.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_10: Alright. I’ll make sure to deliver your brave tale—embellished just enough to suit the young lord’s taste. What is routine for us is nothing more than a fantastical story for them.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_11: Oh, there are a few things worth using. With a bit of embellishment, they should make for a fine tale. Thank you. But... I couldn’t help but notice, just like last time—you’re not exactly gifted at storytelling.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_12: Alright, this is graphic enough—disgustingly so. Now, let’s string it together and wrap it up nicely... Oh, don’t worry too much. I’ll only show just enough. Hopefully, this will make the young lord abandon his foolish dream.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_13: Well, you may not be much of a talker, but your sketches are surprisingly decent. Thank you. They’ll be quite helpful for my next design.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_14: Thank you. Your talents truly shine brightest as an adventurer. Thanks to you, Frost Mountain should be safe for a while. I’ll be able to visit with peace of mind now.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Complete_15: Oh, you really did bring everything you could, didn’t you... First of all, these entrails, the stench is absolutely unbearable. I need to get rid of them before the smell clings to my fabrics. Now, the rest... intriguing, really. The horns have a magnificent curve to them. And this heart, how extraordinary. Cold as carved ice, yet still faintly pulsing. I like it. Get ready. I’m going to create something the world has never seen.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_01: You’ve arrived. Good to see you still standing. I’ve got a dark muse whispering in my ear and a new creation that demands to be brought to life. I need someone I can rely on for this task. Let’s make sure you haven’t grown lazy and soft like the cushions on my settee. We’re not getting any younger, unfortunately.

I heard the news. So it's finally possible to reach the Blue Maelstrom, is it? Perfect timing, really. I've been in need of new materials. Sailors, I’m told, coat cloth with tar to make it waterproof. Could you bring me a sail and some tar? The condition of the sail doesn’t matter. I simply want to examine the texture myself. I’m counting on you.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_02: Lately, I have been repairing more garments than making new ones, especially those worn by adventurers returning from their journeys. If they are damaged to this extent, the cause cannot be ordinary. If you are willing, could you look into it for me? Should you encounter anything dangerous, please take care and bring back anything that might serve as a clue.

Ink is hard to come by, which is why it's usually reserved for fine writing inks. But who’s to say the ink of a cuttlefish from the Blue Maelstrom isn’t something entirely different? If it can be used as a dye, this could be a remarkable discovery.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_03: I looked further into the people returning in such a wretched state. Some of them were spotted near the outskirts of the Forgotten Castle. Could you go and see for yourself what is happening there? Whether it is connected to the curse or not, we need to know. If you come across any traces of slaughter or battle, bring back whatever you can.

I’ve heard rumors of jellyfish in the Blue Maelstrom that give off their own light. They say you can extract a glowing fluid from them if you manage to kill one. Could you get some for me? If I can use that fluid to create luminous fabric, I’ll have the attention and admiration of the upper class in no time!
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_04: I’ve worked with fabric all my life, weaving threads into something stronger. But now? Now the threads of this land are fraying, unraveling. These creatures, this cursed wilderness—there’s something far darker at play here, and it’s not just about survival. It’s about control. They’re being manipulated. If we can cut down the monsters and uncover what they’re hiding, we might be able to stop the unraveling.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_05: Look at you, not quite as tattered as when you first came in, but still showing signs of wear. Don’t ignore it—those ruins don’t just take their toll on your body, they gnaw at your spirit, too. The Shrines of Health should do the trick for now, but you’ve got to keep yourself in one piece if you want to keep moving forward.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_06: Seeing you in this state takes me back to my own beginnings—digging through trash for scraps, with nothing to my name but hunger and desperation. Let’s gather what’s needed, and I’ll help you craft something that leads to a better tomorrow.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_07: Frost Mountain offers more than just cold winds and icy peaks. It holds the promise of timeless beauty, its wintry embrace offering a chance to defy the ravages of time.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_08: Amidst the opulent festivities of high society, I caught wind of troubling news. The rumors of some strange monstrous beasts roaming these lands. You know how most nobility are, don't you? They'll vanish to their countryside estates if we don't address this threat swiftly.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_09: We have an intriguing assignment today. You will be procuring materials so I can craft accessories as part of a covert operation, designed to deceive one of the dark lords. By gaining their favor, we aim to secure access and gather information.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_10: To win the favor of the upper class, one must know plenty of entertaining stories. Young lords, in particular, are especially fond of tales of adventure. One such curious young master has made a rather troublesome request—he wants someone to slay the monsters of Frost Mountain on his behalf and then recount the adventure to him. What do you think? Are you interested? At the very least, the reward will be generous.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_11: Hmm, it seems your tale was well received. This time, the young lord wants to hear about the fascinating locations in Frost Mountain. There’s only so much I can make up on my own, you know. Since we’ve already started this, why don’t you help me out? Explore Frost Mountain thoroughly and find places that are grand, beautiful, or unique enough to make for a good story.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_12: There’s a problem. The young lord enjoyed our stories too much—so much that he now insists on becoming an adventurer! His mother, the lady of the house, is furious! If this keeps up, my connections will be ruined! No, that cannot happen. It’s time to show this naïve young lord a taste of reality.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_13: Frost Mountain truly boasts a breathtaking view. I visited once, long ago, and the Ice Caverns in particular... such mystique, such atmosphere. It stirs the creative fire in artists like myself. Hmm, do you happen to know how to draw? If so, be a dear and sketch the caverns for me, will you? I have a feeling they'll spark some marvelous ideas for my next line.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_14: Looking at your sketches has only confirmed it for me, I simply must see it with my own eyes. But as much as my stitching is impeccable, I must admit, combat isn't exactly my forte. I know it's dangerous, and I’m not foolish enough to charge in unprepared. So how about this, you go on ahead and deal with the monsters for me. I promise the reward will be well worth your while.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Greeting_15: When I visited Frost Mountain, I caught sight of a wendigo in the distance. I used to think all monsters were just hideous brutes, but the wendigo... there’s something different about it. Striking. That peculiar form of its... it might even inspire some patterns or embellishments for a new outfit. Of course, I can’t very well ask you to bring one back alive, so just collect whatever parts you can find. I’ll decide later whether they’re worth using.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Tailor_Title_11_EA: Tales of the Frost Mountain Expedition
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_TavernMaster_Compl: When you put them down, did you feel it? A shift in the air, like something heavy finally lifted? I have a hunch about this. Go visit the Alchemist and tell him I sent you. He might be able to tell you more about what's really going on here. I'll be heading there myself soon enough. There's something stirring in my gut... and it's not the ale.

I’ve taken a look at what you brought back, and there doesn’t seem to be anything wrong with it. It smells fine, and it even seems fit to eat. All the more strange. What kind of magic could be at work in that cursed castle...

This map... it’s got history. Every mark on it tells of a time before everything fell apart. Maybe one day, I’ll tell you all about it over a drink... or perhaps over something stronger. But for now, the map is yours.
You’ve done well, but don’t relax just yet. There’s a long road ahead, and the challenges will only grow harder. The tavern’s packed at the moment—swing by later when things settle.

Well done. Those mages won’t be casting their spells again, and the champion’s fallen, as expected. But don’t let your guard down just yet. Had a strange visitor the other night—he was covered in blood and wore a necklace with freshly cut, bloody fingers. When he saw me looking, he quickly covered himself with his cloak, ate, and left. We’ll talk more later; never know who’s listening.

Good to see you back. The wenches? Still laid up with something, and I’m starting to think it’s more than just food poisoning. Things have quieted down for now, so I’m thinking of paying the Surgeon another visit. Hopefully, he’s got something that’ll get them back on their feet—customers are a lot more satisfied when there are busty women to serve them.
Impressive! These gleaming gems will do the trick. The Collector will be satisfied, and you’ve more than earned your compensation.

The evidence you uncovered paints a grim picture of what’s happening. The ritualistic marks, the suffering... But if the rumors are true, and someone or something is devouring their souls, I wonder... Come back soon. I need to look into something.

The wraith is gone, but sadly, no change in the living. I’ll need to do some research and figure out what our next move should be. Come back soon; we’ll need to plan more precisely and carefully than when I’m balancing the books.

One of the bodies did indeed bear markings similar to those we’ve encountered before—though they seem slightly different. This suggests a deeper, darker evolution of whatever is at play. We’re not done yet, though. I’ll need more time to piece these findings together. Come back soon.

Good work. This is a solid start, but it won’t be enough to clear all the debts left behind by the dead. We’ll need more, but at least we’re on the right path. For now, this will help begin the process of easing their suffering.

Good work. The families have asked me to express their gratitude. One even baked you a Chocolate Chip Muffin as a token of thanks. Unfortunately, I seem to have misplaced it... though I swear I didn’t eat it. In any case, the silver and other valuables you’ve brought will make a real difference.

The chalice you’ve brought back is undeniably foul, a palpable darkness clinging to it like a stain. But is it the one we need? I’ll send it to someone more skilled in these matters to confirm our findings. In the meantime, I’ve been informed of other pressing issues that will require your attention sooner rather than later.

The information you gathered was a great help to my contact. However, there is still much left to uncover. The truth is drawing ever closer, but it will take more time to fully understand the significance of what we are dealing with. The next step of this journey lies just ahead, so return to me soon.

What was found in the armory has revealed far more than we expected. Yet this is only the beginning. What we have uncovered is merely a piece of the puzzle, and it is likely that the answers lie hidden somewhere deeper. There is a door that has been sealed for far too long. When you are ready, we must face whatever lies beyond it together.
I’ll make sure word gets around that you’re not someone to be trifled with. Come by for a drink sometime, you’ve earned more than just the coin.
Back already? You look frozen solid! Go thaw out by the fire while I fetch you something to warm you up from the inside—my own recipe.
The search party should be in safer hands now. Come on back and take a seat. I’ve got some hearty stew waiting for you—warm you up after all that cold. You’ve earned it.

We’ve learned what we can for now, but we can’t afford to stop here. The darkness is spreading, and we need more information to understand how to break this curse. Time is slipping away. One of my wenches... she’s gone. Choked on her own blood and bile. The others may not be far behind. We need to press on, gather more answers before it’s too late for them—before it’s too late for all of us.

The priest who tried to help her is now infected. We had no choice but to put him down before he could do any more harm. This is no ordinary curse. I cannot help but wonder if it might be something else entirely. Regardless, your findings have given us a new lead, and that is something we can build upon.

The Lich's involvement is undeniable. He was the king's most trusted, and from the evidence you have gathered, it appears he played a much larger role in this curse than we ever imagined. However, the details remain unclear. We must dig deeper, and at the same time, focus on preparing for the battles ahead. Visit me soon, adventurer. We must inform the others of our findings and plan our next move.
I didn’t think you had it in you... you really do know your way around down there. Don’t go too far, I will be needing your skills again soon.
That chest held everything I imagined and more! If you find yourself a few more chests like that, you might become the richest adventurer in town!
I knew you would find it, but I didn’t expect you to be so quick! I hope this reward is fair compensation for your tremendous effort.

I know what you're capable of, but the miner wanted to be certain. Felt bad about dragging someone like you into such dangerous business. Still, seeing you back in one piece should put his mind at ease.

The miner's face fell when I told him nothing was found. Though if you ask me, I'm relieved. At least there were no bodies to speak of. Bad news has a way of weighing on the one who delivers it, not just the one who receives it.
Not one of them with their senses intact. I had a feeling it might come to this, but hearing it said aloud sits heavy with me. I'm not sure how to break it to him.
I tell ya, that feeling of spiritual clarity after receiving a good ol' blessing is hard to beat!
You’ve returned safely. Seeing this, I know you dealt with those fiends for certain. Your skill is truly remarkable. I celebrate your victory and grant you a reward worthy of it.
Tonight we celebrate! Let’s drink to your health and fortunes!

The navigator stopped by to say the timber was good quality. Sturdy enough that it shouldn't break easily, and she's already started on the deck and hull. Says there's still more work to be done, so I may have another favor to ask of you soon, if you're willing.
She was pleased with what you brought. Said the fabric was thick and sturdy, more than fit for the sea. Just a little more work, she says, and the ship will be ready to sail.

The navigator says the ship is ready. Anyone who sails near the Blue Maelstrom must know what they're doing, so she's clearly the real thing. If you ever find yourself needing to cross the sea, she's the one to look for.

I passed along the news to the navigator. She sat quietly with her drink for a while, then asked me to give you her thanks. Said it felt like a small part of an old debt had been repaid. I sense she’s got something weighing on her she hasn’t shared. Then again, most of the folks who walk through my door do.

I passed along what you found to the navigator. She reckoned it was likely remnants from sunken ships. Keepsakes, she called them, traces of those who never made it back. Meant more to her than she let on, I think.

Sounds like she means to avenge her fallen crewmates. Leaving the fleet to run her own merchant vessel seems to be part of that plan. After all, hiring someone of your skill doesn't come cheap. Adventurer, I hope you'll see her through this.
I feel much safer now that you’ve cleared out a bunch of their kind. Take a seat by the fire and take a well deserved rest.
I knew I could count on you. The Collector's debt is settled, and as promised, here's something for your trouble.
Bravo! You’ve conquered the Frost Mountain’s deadliest foes. Come, have a drink with me. I’ve prepared a brew that’s as legendary as your deeds.
Excellent! With each haul from the chests, you grow significantly wealthier. You may soon become the richest adventurer of all.
You’ve truly found it! When I first sent you on this journey, I never believed the legends were real. Yet here you are, proving me wrong—and bringing a myth to life.
These are perfect! How did you manage to find bangles in this condition? You really have a knack for getting the good stuff.

Well done. Though it's a sorry state of affairs. The dwarves were once said to be the finest handlers of fire there ever were, and now they must fight it to reclaim their peace. I hope they find their way back to ordinary days soon, but I don't imagine it'll be easy.
Bodies already reduced to bone. That's a strange and troubling thing. It seems Ignir is corrupting everything in that place. We must stop him before it is too late.

Well done, truly. Thanks to you, Ignir's influence has been pushed back, if only for a short while. But the miner says he can always create new servants, so we'd best start preparing for what comes next.

Thanks to you, the scouting should go more smoothly for a while. From what I gather, she's been looking for her brother's map. Says it was taken when the pirates captured her. Believes it's somewhere in the Ship Graveyard.

Her brother was an archaeologist, it seems. The two of them had been searching for ancient ruins and forgotten sea routes together. Promised each other to set sail and explore once they found something with potential. Now she's on her own. Some stories never get easier to hear, no matter how often they're told.
A fortress-like structure, you say? I'll pass that along to her. I can't say what it means, but I hope it turns out to be something worth looking into. For her sake, and her brother's.

When I brought her the journal you found, she wept for quite some time. Said it belonged to her crewmate, sure enough. Apparently he was a curious sort, always jotting down whatever caught his interest. She asked me to pass along her thanks for bringing it back. I'll add my own as well.

The pearl and coral from the Blue Maelstrom are something else, I'll give them that. Strange color and texture, unlike anything you'd find elsewhere. From what I can tell, she means to bring these along with the journal to her crewmate's family. A decent thing to do, if you ask me.

Turns out the navigator has an ancient compass of sorts. Place something on it and it points to wherever that thing is connected. She put the eye you brought on it and her expression changed. Said it was pointing to a land abandoned long ago. A place where the river dried up, the earth turned foul, and nothing lives there now. Says she means to investigate it soon.

I hope you found something of value. I trust in your skill, but I have seen far too many adventurers who relied solely on their abilities, only to never return. I hope to continue seeing you at my tavern, so always ensure you are well-prepared.

Was there nothing unusual? I see... Actually, I’ve heard that an Alchemist has been searching for something lately. As you know, Alchemists will do anything in the name of their experiments—whether for good or ill, it hardly matters to them. This time, he’s looking for a particular item, and I find that concerning... If I find out what exactly he seeks, I will let you know.

This seems to be the one. It’s a relief that you found it first. Please keep this matter a secret from the Alchemist. I know he has accomplished remarkable things and has helped many people, but I worry that one day, he may cross a line he cannot return from. I only hope that day never comes.
Thank you for checking. Sounds like their weapons aren't in as good a shape as we'd thought, and they don't appear to be hiding much either. I'll see that the navigator hears all of this.
Well done, truly. Hearing this should bring the navigator some measure of peace. Just one step left now. She says she still has one last thing to ask of you, so don't disappear on us.

I passed along the news to the navigator straight away. She sat quietly for a long while, then spoke. Said she hoped her fallen crewmates could finally rest in peace. Asked me to give you her sincerest thanks. I reckon she can put the past behind her now and start living for herself. Have a seat, friend. First drink's on me tonight.
The miner's eyes sharpened when I told him the flow of fire was unstable. Said it means Ignir's power is being spread thin. We need to move quickly, he says.
Well done. The miner says all the preparations that can be made have been made. With those who aid Ignir lying low, now is the time to act. Come back when you're ready.

Well done, adventurer. The miner says a spirit like Ignir doesn't fade so easily. He's likely hiding within the lava, waiting for another chance. He means to find a way to seal him completely before he can recover his strength. He also asked me to pass along his thanks. Here, drink up. Tonight's ale is on him.

Well done. Do not take lesser demons lightly. There is no end to them. Cut one down and another soon takes its place. Truth be told, the worst of it is that there is no time to rest. Still, thanks to you, we can catch our breath tonight.
You have done well. Judging by the look on your face, they were no easy prey. Still, you have returned alive. There is no better news than that.

You made it back alive. That is a relief. The demons are not gone, but we have at least bought ourselves a moment to breathe. Thanks to you, we may sleep in some peace tonight. Get your rest while you can, adventurer. This fight will not end easily.

I knew you’d pull it off. You’ve done a great job, truly. More than anything, I’m glad you made it back in one piece. Come now, have a seat. Let me pour you a pint of the finest ale in all the realm. Once you've had a good swig, tell me your tale from the Inferno.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_TavernMaster_Greet: Once, those skeletons were men, brave warriors who swore to protect this kingdom. But the king's hunger for darkness twisted everything. Their souls were bound by a curse, left to wander without rest. There is a prophecy, they say, that a 'chosen one' will break the curse and grant them peace. I once believed I could be that person, but it proved to be a difficult path. Regardless, someone must put an end to this curse. Whether that someone is you or not... there's no harm in trying.

That old castle should hold nothing but rot, yet food and drink still turn up there. Fresh fruit, even meals that are still warm, are not something to brush aside. If you find anything like that in the castle, bring it to me. And whatever you do, do not try eating it yourself.

I seem to have misplaced something important, something more than just paper and ink... a map, to be exact. It once led me to places I preferred to forget, but now I need it. The forgotten castle might still hold the answers, or perhaps more nightmares. Think you can find it in that cursed place?

Ah, you’ve returned. I paid a visit to our friend, but we’ll need a few things before we can move forward. It’s the first of many trials, if you can call them that. Gather what’s needed, and we’ll see where this leads. If you succeed, we’ll talk about the next step—but let’s not get ahead of ourselves, eh? One thing at a time.

I’ve got another task for you, and it won’t be pretty. The mages—they’ll tear through your defenses if you’re not careful. As for the champion... well, if you make it back, you’ll understand why they call it that. Take them down, and we’ll have one less obstacle standing between us and the truth. Keep your head on straight—this one's going to test your patience.

Good to see you back in one piece. Things are a mess around here—my wenches have all come down with something, and I’m starting to think it’s not just the roasted rabbit from the other night. In times like this, it’s always smart to have a backup plan. You never know when you’ll need a quick exit.

The Collector lost badly in a wager with the Goblin Merchant, and now the debt has fallen to me. I suppose that is the price of an old favor I once owed him. To settle it, I’ll need a few valuables. Bring them to me, and I promise a reward worthy of your effort.

Greetings. I have been kept busy lately, tending to the belongings of adventurers who passed through the tavern and never returned. It is a task that never gets easier, no matter how much time goes by. But what troubles me more is what these poor souls endured. Branded, tortured like animals, left to perish in silence until death finally claimed them. One of my regulars has given me a lead. They believe they know where their loved one was last found. I think we should investigate.

You’re back. Good. I’ve been mulling over something—rumors of creatures that devour souls. The wraiths are the first of many, I suspect. If we slay them, perhaps the souls trapped in this cycle will find rest. And if we’re lucky, those still living might snap out of whatever trance they’re in. It’s a long shot, but it’s a start.

Rumors suggest that the bodies within may have been among the first to be subjected to the same ritualistic torment as those more recent poor souls. Search for any clues—check if their tongues were severed or if strange markings are carved into their flesh. We can’t be sure until we investigate. If there’s any connection, we need to understand it before this spreads further.

When I think of those poor souls and their families, left to bear the weight of debts they never agreed to, my heart grows heavy. It is a cruel irony that the dead leave behind not only sorrow but financial ruin. I wish to help free them, but to do so we must gather the necessary funds. Bring me some silver coins, and we can begin to ease their suffering.

Nice to see you again. The families are starting to feel the weight lift, and I’m hoping there’s something of real value hidden inside those Mimics. Whatever we find could go a long way in easing their suffering.

I’ve heard whispers—dark rumors—of a chalice, one used in the first rituals. It’s said to lie hidden in the Forgotten Castle, a relic of blood and shadows. I don’t need to tell you that it’s no ordinary artifact. It’s something far darker. Something that could give us the answers we desperately seek, or drag us deeper into this abyss. I need you to find it before it’s too late. The darkness is spreading, and we need to understand what secrets it holds before they consume us all.

I have been informed that there were many pieces used in the original ceremony beyond the chalice you found. My contact is still digging deeper, but some of these missing pieces may lie at the altar within the Crypt. We will need to clear out any undead protectors lingering there before we can get close to the truth. Once you have dealt with the threats inside, come see me.

There is one more thing we must uncover. According to my contact's investigation, there is a possibility that traces of the ritual remain within the armory of the Forgotten Castle. Go and see for yourself what lies hidden there. Do not overlook any markings, symbols, or relics engraved on weapons or armor. Every detail could prove to be a vital clue.

Word around the tavern is that some frost-bitten creatures have been roaming the outskirts, freezing everything in their path. I’ve got an old friend who might know a way to deal with them, but he needs some muscle first. If you’re willing to brave the cold, I’ll see you’re compensated properly. Just don’t let those icy bastards catch you off guard.

Now that you've got some experience under your belt, I’ve got a task that’ll put your skills to the test. We need to check the escape routes—make sure they're clear and ready in case things go south. It's cold out there, though, so make sure you bundle up. Last thing I need is for you to catch a chill... or worse.

Ready to face some real danger? We’ve got frost-covered fiends lurking in the shadows of Frost Mountain. A search party’s heading up to look for that missing girl, and they could use some backup. I need you to help clear the way, make sure they’re not walking into a death trap.

Something has been shifting in the shadows lately, and I am not the only one who has noticed. The tavern, once brimming with chatter and laughter, is growing quieter by the day. Even my staff have fallen ill with a strange sickness I cannot explain. Some say the darkness is coming from the Forgotten Castle. The brothers have suggested we investigate the matter there. Will you lend us your help?

The situation is growing dire. As they were preparing the body of my deceased staff member for burial, she came back to life! But she was not the same. She attacked anyone who came near, even tearing a chunk out of one of the priests. This... this is the nightmare we are dealing with. We must continue looking into the origins of this curse and find a way to stop it.

We must proceed carefully and find solid evidence before drawing conclusions. The Lich was once the king's most loyal court wizard, and from everything we have uncovered so far, it seems he may have had a much larger role in this than we first suspected. Search the Forgotten Castle and bring back anything that proves his involvement. Only then can we begin to prepare our next move.
Deep below The Forgotten Castle lies an iron door sealed shut. It is known to be heavily guarded... but the reason why is still unknown. I need you to go find out what that reason might be.

Rumors of a grand chest filled with blessed riches have echoed around these parts for years... but after hearing some tavern talk, I am convinced I know where it sits. If you think you have what it takes, I will guide you on your way to open it once and for all!

It seems you have proven your ability to explore the more dangerous parts of that castle. Now I must seek an item once used in a ritual. However, its quality and condition must be excellent. The deeper you go, the easier it will be to find such a thing.

A dwarf miner came into my tavern not long ago. Hadn't seen one of his kind in quite some time, and he was covered in wounds. Said they made a grave mistake and unleashed a calamity of fire upon their land. He managed to escape, but many of his kin are still held there, bound under its control. He's looking for someone capable of helping him. Said he needs a proven hand. Would you be willing to take the job?

The miner says he had companions with him when he fled his homeland. They got separated in the chaos, and he's heard nothing from them since. He's looking for someone to go and search for any trace of them. Says it's a place of intense heat, but their dwarven shrines should help make things more manageable. I'm asking on his behalf.

The miner has asked me to pass along another request. He says Ignir, the calamity of fire, has seized control of his kin by eroding their minds. But if even one of them still has their senses, he wants them brought back. There may be fighting involved. He understands that, and so should you.
The fact that you’re still in one piece tells me the god’s are looking out fer ya. Might be a good idea to show your appreciation and offer some blessings at the shrines.
Would it not be a waste to squander the blessings of the gods within a tavern? I know of some demons who are well deserving of divine retribution. Hunt them down and bring me the proof.

The number of monsters within the Forgotten Castle continues to grow. Many adventurers strive to cleanse that place, yet it seems impossible to drive away the darkness entirely... Still, we cannot abandon this fight. Their numbers must be thinned. Defeat them and show me proof of your deeds. It will not be easy, but I ask this of you.

A sailor stopped by my tavern not long ago. Said she was a navigator, looking for someone to help her repair an old ship. Wants to get her sailing again as a merchant vessel. She asked if I knew anyone suitable, and you came to mind. If you're interested, bring her some sturdy timber and that should get things started.

Turns out she used to sail with a large merchant fleet. Left the work behind and spent her savings on that old ship. Something happened, I reckon, though she didn't say more than that. Either way, she still needs a hand. This time it's a new sail she's after. Bring her some sturdy cloth and a set of sewing tools if you can.

That navigator talks about ships at great length every time she comes in. Most of it goes over my head, but I make sure to remember the parts that matter. This time she needs rope. Says there's no end to how much a ship gets through, so she needs some extra on hand. I told her I knew just the person to ask.

Seems like pirates are to sailors what monsters are to adventurers. The Black Despair crew in particular have quite a reputation. Plundered countless ships and left a trail of bodies behind them. The navigator said they're the reason she left the fleet. She's looking for someone to deal with them. Adventurer, I'm asking on her behalf.

Apparently there are large structures scattered across the Ship Graveyard, shaped like giant shells. Sailors call them mermaid coffins, though no one knows what lies inside. The navigator's brother once studied them. She wants to know the truth, if only for his sake. Would you take a look inside one for her?

The navigator opened up a little last night. Said she's been looking for someone with both the fighting skill and the survival instinct to see her through what's ahead. Someone who could help her settle a score. She asked about you, and I told her the best way to find out was to see for herself. If you're willing to help her, go show her what you're capable of.
The skeleton army has been wreaking havoc up on that snowy peak. Can you get a handle on them before they become an even greater threat?
I owe the Collector a debt but I can’t just leave the tavern. Can you collect the items for me and I’ll make it worth your while.

Demonic forces have made their abode deep within the heart of the frost mountain. To top it off they’ve captured a terrifying frost wyvern. Who knows that terrible plans they intend to use that beast for. We need to take them out before they can spring into action.

As you prepare for the battles ahead, remember this. It is not only your weapons and armor that need strengthening, but your coffers as well! The unexpected is always part of any adventure. Having a little extra coin on hand will put your mind at ease when that time comes.
I have heard stories of a stone door deep below The Forgotten Castle... It is said to hold unimaginable legendary treasures, so, how does a hunt sound?

Recently, more people have been searching for bangles of exceptional quality. Do you happen to know where such things might be found? If fortune favors you, you may find them among the piles of treasure in that haunted castle. But be careful. You will not be the only one searching for them.

The miner tells me Ignir has twisted not only his kin, but the beasts of that land as well. The flame boars in particular were once animals they raised themselves, but now they wander through the fires without reason, driven to rage. Leave them be and they'll become a greater threat. Put them down and bring back what remains as proof.

Word has come from those who recently passed through the miner's homeland. They found bodies of his kin there. When he escaped, they were under Ignir's control, but alive. What happened in the time between, I couldn't say. Please go and check on the condition of the fallen.

According to the miner, his enthralled kin have been digging without rest. The lava fields have spread as a result, and a lava golem has emerged. He says it's as good as a thrall of Ignir himself. The stronger Ignir's influence grows, the stronger the golem becomes. Take it down before things get any worse.

Word came in from the navigator's scouting party. They've been having trouble with the Tidewalkers near the Ship Graveyard. Apparently those creatures attack without hesitation the moment they spot an enemy, and the ones running with a shaman are even worse. Looks like they could use a hand. Would you be willing to step in?

I've got good news and bad news. The good news is that part of the map she's been looking for has turned up. The bad news is that it isn't enough. She still needs the remaining pieces, but with monsters and pirates prowling that area, the search has hit a wall. Would you be willing to track down the rest of the map?

The navigator found a spot marked for investigation on the restored map, somewhere deeper in the Ship Graveyard. Likely her brother's doing, she thinks. She wants to know what's there. Adventurer, I'm asking on her behalf.

I heard some of her story the other day. When the pirates took her ship, most of her crew were thrown overboard. She was the only one who made it out. A sorry thing. There are tales of man-eating fish in the waters of the Blue Maelstrom. Deal with them if you can, and if you come across anything that might have belonged to a sailor, bring it back. I'd like to pass it along to her, just in case.

She’s had her head in that journal every waking minute. Came to see me this morning with something she'd found inside. Says there are pearls that shine without sun or torch, and coral twisted into shapes that shouldn't be. She wants to find them in memory of her lost crewmate. Adventurer, would you bring back the pearl and coral for her?

The navigator showed me something from her brother's research notes yesterday. Spoke of a great river that once existed and a guardian said to dwell within it. Most of it was speculation, but the description of the guardian was hard to ignore. A beast with massive jaws, a vertical eye, and thick leathery skin. She thinks it might be connected to the Crocodilian. Hunt them down and bring back one of their eyes, if you would.

What do you believe ensures safety in an adventure? Skill, of course, is essential. But when skill levels are equal, what makes the difference? Superior equipment. Unfortunately, while decent gear is easy to find here, truly exceptional equipment is rare. In truth, many such treasures lie buried deep within the Forgotten Castle, hidden among hoards of riches. You should seek them out.

Do you remember the stone door you opened last time? Now that we know for certain that treasures lie beyond such doors, we must investigate the rumors of other sealed passages as well. Open them and see what lies beyond. And... if you come across any treasure that carries a strange aura, be sure to let me know.

I’ve discovered what the Alchemist is searching for—a cursed crown. No matter what is done to it, it remains unscathed, and the gemstone at its center glows even in complete darkness. Can you find it before he does? I do not know what curse it carries, but this time, the Alchemist must not be allowed to obtain it. I have a bad feeling about this.

The navigator's scouting parties have been combing through the Ship Graveyard, but it’s rough out there. She needs someone to go in and take a closer look at the places the pirates frequent. Would you be willing to help? They're not to be underestimated, so watch yourself.

According to the navigator, the Black Despair pirates are blindly loyal to their captain. Long fancied themselves masters of the sea, plundering and burning countless ships along the way. Her ship likely met that same fate. Those wretches have a debt to pay. Adventurer, please help her see that they do.

There isn't a sailor alive who hasn't heard of Captain Bladehand, or so they say. The navigator told me she's been waiting for this day ever since she survived his attack. Says everything is in place now, and she's asking you to finish it.

The miner wants to assess Ignir's condition before confronting him directly. He's asking you to look into the area around the great forge and observe the flames and the flow of the lava. Says that with Ignir pouring his strength into expanding his control, he can't be maintaining perfect command over everything. Find that opening.

The miner says the fire spirits and elementals are what help Ignir recover his strength. They act as conduits, gathering the power of fire and delivering it to him. Leave them be and the scattered power will come together again before long. He's asking you to take them out and slow that process down. Adventurer, I'm asking on his behalf.

Dwarf legend has it that Ignir in his true form is a being made solely of living lava. But with the seal broken incompletely, he now bears the form of a fire colossus, solid stone entwined with molten fire. The miner says we must stop him before he reclaims that true form. Adventurer, please put an end to him.

The lower reaches of the Forgotten Castle have already become a den of demons. The trouble is, their numbers are not thinning but growing still. If this keeps on, they will start crawling upward soon enough. We need to act before that happens. There is no need to go too deep. Just start thinning out the ones in plain sight.

I have heard rumors of a creature unlike the common run of demons. The details are still uncertain, but one thing is clear. It is a far harsher foe than any you have faced so far. While the demons we have seen until now were little more than raging beasts, this creature operates with malicious purpose. Judge with care, and do not overreach.

There is one that commands the demons. You might call it the one that governs the Inferno. Many adventurers have tried to slay the odious overseer, but all have failed. In the past, I would not have sat idle upon hearing this. But I am no longer in a body that can answer such a call. So I would entrust this to the one I trust most. Adventurer, I ask this of you.

More demons have appeared deep within the Forgotten Castle. And we still don’t even know what’s causing the plague. Things aren't looking good. If this keeps up, something far worse could be waiting for us. Adventurer, please. Put an end to those demons from the Inferno.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_TavernMaster_Title: The Cloth That Wraps the Wind
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_TavernMaster_Tuto_: Well done. You can tell at a glance whether someone is a prepared adventurer or just pretending by how they deal with the undead. You are the real thing.
I hope you found something worthwhile. Those who come back with decent loot usually return here for an ale. If you have a little coin to spare, why not have a drink yourself.
You made it back without injury. That is good to see. With this level of skill, I can trust you with proper contracts from here on.

Welcome. If you are looking for information or companions, you have come to the right place. This is where adventurers and rumors tend to gather. But information often comes with danger. I do not give work to just anyone. If you want a contract, show me what you can do.

There are more useful items in a dungeon than you might expect, including things you can obtain without having to fight every monster. If I were to offer one piece of advice, do not pass by the small chests in the old castle. Take a closer look, and you may find something better than you expected.

As you know, the old castle is a dangerous place. With a bit of luck, you might find valuable gear or coin. But none of it matters unless you make it back alive. Adventurer, explore the Forgotten Castle and return safely.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_TheCollector_Compl: Fantastic. You’ve done well. Now, go ahead and rest up; I’m sure you’ve earned it. Come see me soon when you’re ready to continue. We’re not done yet.
These are just the pieces I needed. There’s still much more to gather, but go ahead and thaw out. When you're ready, come back for the next task. We’re far from finished.

Good. I will see that these are delivered properly. The Fortune Teller and I sometimes seek things that may seem a little peculiar to others. But I do not concern myself with what people say. We know exactly what it is we must do.

The true worth of an object shines only in the hands of one who can recognize it. This one is no different. Thanks to you, I have obtained it, and you shall have your rightful reward. You have done well.
How intriguing. Frost Giants are guarding the place. There must be something there that we have yet to discover. With continued investigation, I am certain we will uncover its secrets one day.
Thank you. One of your finer qualities is that you do not ask how or where I intend to use these things. Now then, here is your compensation.
My my, you’ve proven your strength. I shouldn’t have underestimate you.

My word! Bound in ropes and sunk beneath the waves, you say? Remarkable. This could be compelling evidence that something from the merfolk legend truly happened. Were they truly sacrifices, just as the stories claim? Or is there another truth we’ve yet to uncover? Fascinating. That place certainly deserves a closer investigation.

Truly impressive. It's been some time since I've seen an adventurer of your skill. I hope you won't take offense. This wasn't meant as a test. But after watching so many missions end in bitter failure, I'm sure you can understand my caution. In any case, you've earned my trust now, and I intend to reward you accordingly.
Well done. Thanks to you, we’ll be able to continue our investigation without trouble for a while. Here, take this. I hope it serves as a reward worthy of your efforts.
You’re proving more and more valuable to me. I’ll be sure to call on you when I have another interesting deal.

These scales have such a strange and mesmerizing hue. And this tear, this translucent droplet-shaped crystal, expands my view once more despite all the gems I’ve collected over the years. It is truly a breathtaking beauty.
That’s pretty impressive. Those beasts weren’t pushovers. Hope these items make up for your time.
Hope you didn’t get a hangover. Here’s a few coin to help you recover.
Hmm, some of these are a bit bloody, but no worries, I'll have them cleaned up in no time.
Let’s see what secrets I can uncover with these artifacts. I’ll let you know if I discover anything. In the meantime, here have these items.
Hmm I’m starting to notice a pattern. I think a few more pieces and I’ll have unraveled their origin.
Ah ha! That bowl was the missing link! This is all very interesting. Hmmm... a land lost to the sea. I apologize. I’m getting ahead of myself.
As I suspected, they are quite different from ordinary bats. Living in a place where lava flows, I expected them to possess some unusual traits, but this exceeds even my expectations.

So this is the vocal sac. It expands far more than I expected. I can only imagine how loud the creature must be when it is alive. Hmm... perhaps next time I should find someone willing to bring me one alive.

It is far more beautiful than I had imagined from the rumors alone. After all, something cannot truly be said to be yours until you have held it in your own hands. There are still many things in this world that stir my curiosity. I look forward to seeing what other fascinating treasures you bring me in the future.
Oh, this is unmistakably different. It goes far beyond anything described in the records. Discoveries like this are why I cannot stop collecting. Your reward, as promised. You have my thanks.
Oh, do take a look at this. Scorched and fouled… I cannot tell what this is made of. It does not seem to be ordinary iron… Best to have a specialist examine it.

I am no expert, but the aura that lingers in this fragment is unmistakably strange. The longer I look at it… the more it stirs an unease I cannot quite explain. And yet, for those such as myself, it is precisely such objects that hold the greatest value.

Oh... this is truly of great worth. I cannot deny that not only your skill, but also your eye for rarity grows keener with each step. Since you have brought me such a treasure, I shall grant you something special in return. And should you uncover more marvels in your journey ahead, be sure to bring them to me.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_TheCollector_Greet: As always, I’m after something valuable, but this land is plagued with these beasts—Frost Wolves. I need you to thin them out, clear the path, so I can get what I’m after without being interrupted by these vile creatures.

I have quite a long list of curious items I’m pursuing, but we’ll start with these. They may not seem like much on their own, but I assure you, they will help complete my collection. Once you bring them to me, I’ll entrust you with the next request.

I received a request from the Fortune Teller, but of course she asked for an item I passed on to another collector not long ago. I have a few favors to ask of her myself, and I would rather not lose her goodwill over something so trivial. I will need to acquire it again. Would you help me? It should not be too difficult to find.

Objects found within dungeons may seem common, yet they are never truly ordinary. At times, the essence of the land or its creatures seeps into them, transforming them into something entirely different. Of course, most may be discarded, but if even the slightest possibility lies within... is that not worth the attempt?

Did you know there is a river within Frost Mountain that never freezes? Stranger still, rafts of unknown origin are said to drift along its waters from time to time. They say anyone who boards one can safely make their way back out. Such a curious phenomenon cannot simply be ignored. Would you take a look for me?

You may not know it, but I place a fair amount of trust in you. I believe that, no matter how strange an item I ask for, you would see it done. This request is no different. It is no different from the tasks I have asked of you before. Now then, would you bring me a few items?
I apologize for being so terse. I get a little antsy when working on my secret projects. Anyways, I have another task that can lead to riches. Start off by eradicating the undead in the mountains.

Long ago, the merfolk are said to have offered themselves as sacrifices to calm the fury of the sea after committing a great wrong. Most dismiss it as an old tale, but I do not. Did you know there were once far more merfolk than there are today? There must be a hidden truth behind it. I want you to find out whether a merfolk grave truly exists within the Blue Maelstrom.

This time, the task will be a bit more difficult. The yetis of Frost Mountain resemble apes, but they are far larger. Despite their massive size, they are incredibly swift and cunning. If you can bring that creature down, I’ll be willing to consider a new offer.

I assembled a team to investigate the Blue Maelstrom, but their progress is slower than a slug. They say the merfolk there attack without hesitation. And to make matters worse, even the ones thought to be dead have begun to move again. I need your help. Deal with those wretched things, would you?
What I’d give to have a trophy of those ferocious beasts up on the mountains. Get me what I need an I’ll make it worthwhile.

It’s well known that merfolk lure people with their enchanting songs. But what fascinates me more is the merfolk themselves. Their shimmering, iridescent scales and the crystals known as mermaid’s tears. The tears in particular are said to form at the very moment their breath leaves them, like a final scream. What do you say, adventurer? If you can bring these to me, I promise the reward will not disappoint.
Been getting reports of some terrible beasts up on the mountain harassing my kin. Can you do a favor and take them out?
Heard it’s getting pretty cold up in the peaks. Nothing warms the body like a few good ales and taking out skeletons.
I got another peculiar request. I need a few items that only come from the terrible creatures up on that frost mountain. Get them for me and I’ll be sure to make up for your time.
I’ve heard on good authority that some old relics are more than what they seem. If there’s one thing I can’t resist, it’s a good mystery.
Those pieces you brought were just the tip of the iceberg. It looks like the rarer relics hold similar secrets. Can you check some of the more valuable chests for similar relics?
I know this next list of items is a little strange, but trust me, I’m getting close to discovering the secret of the relics.

Molten Bats are a common sight throughout Firedeep. Yet when I looked through my collection, I realized I did not have a single item related to them. The more I think about it, the more regrettable that seems. Hunt them down and bring me something to remember them by.

I have heard that the toads living in Firedeep produce loud and peculiar calls. Some adventurers even complain that the noise keeps them from getting any proper rest. I cannot help but wonder if there is something unusual about their anatomy. Hunt down the Blaze Toads and bring me a few of their vocal sacs.

There have been rumors of a butterfly in Firedeep with wings like living flames. They say its wings are wreathed in fire, yet never burn away. If the stories are true, it would make a truly valuable addition to my collection. Bring me one of those wings.

Thanks to the efforts of many adventurers, items tied to demons have become rather easy to obtain of late. As a result, much has already been studied. Such things do not interest me. I seek what no one truly knows, what has yet to be properly understood. An adventurer like you should be able to find such things, would you not? I will see that you are well rewarded.

Those who have ventured into the lower reaches of the Forgotten Castle all speak of its foul air. Yet within it, the demons move unharmed, even wielding gear not unlike our own. I wonder what sets their equipment apart from ours. Would you bring me something they used? It need not be intact.

Wings are usually seen as little more than a bodily organ. Yet in the world of demons, it is said they carry a different meaning. Not merely for movement, but a display of the power they wield and the rank they hold. If that is true, would not the wings of a stronger demon bear something… distinct?

Adventurer, there are many like me who seek rare and elusive relics. Such a pursuit is no mere pastime, but a noble path of inquiry. Ancient legends, hidden treasures, remnants of the past, traces of monsters... anything will do. Bring me what is truly rare, and you shall be handsomely rewarded.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Valentine_Daily_Co: We may not be able to stop the spreading plague all at once, but if everyone lends their strength as you have, it will buy us time to restore the balance of love. Please, take this rose. It once bloomed in darkness, but through purification, it has regained its true fragrance. A living testament that, with love, anything can be restored.
I know it wasn’t easy, but your courage will pave the way forward. Sometimes, love spreads through the most unexpected paths.
This is exactly what I needed to know. Our combined efforts are working. If we keep this up, love will surely prevail.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Valentine_Daily_Gr: The season of love has come... yet the air is still filled with death. Skeletons, goblins, kobolds... the plague is spreading to everything that moves. For now, ending those who carry it seems to be the only way to slow its spread. I sincerely ask for your help.
Even the strongest creatures are not immune to this plague. Many adventurers avoid the riskiest encounters, but someone must face them. If you lead the way, I will make sure the risk is worth it.
I have yet to measure the true extent of this rot. Search everywhere you can. We must continue to monitor the situation.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Valentine_Seasonal: It may not be a grand reward, but if you continue to help keep this plague at bay, I will find a way to offer you something better.
I know it was no easy task, but I hope this reward brings you some small comfort. As long as we do not give up, we will surely see this through.
You have taken the lead in restoring the balance of love through your efforts. You are truly a Bringer of Love. I hope this gift can repay you for all that you have done.

The Black Rose has become a symbol of resistance against this plague. Once steeped in darkness, it has now been fully purified, bearing a new kind of beauty and fragrance. Bring me one, and I will reward you for your effort.

You are clearly making a difference, Adventurer. As more people join you in purpose, we will be able to overcome this trial all the sooner. As a token of that journey, would you bring me three Black Roses?

There is no defeat for the power of love. If you can gather ten Black Roses, that alone will stand as a great sign of encouragement in this arduous fight. It may take time, but I ask that you see it through to the very end.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Weaponsmith_Comple: Your hands tell the story... so don’t bother telling it to me. Here, these might make it easier for you next time!
Wow... and here I was thinking how ridiculous that sounded. Those Ruins are getting more dangerous by the day.
You brought these a lot faster than I expected... I guess you were prepared. If you come back later I might be able to craft something special for you.

These weapons will work. With them, I can begin the real work, but there’s more to this story. My great-grandfather spoke of an ancient sword hidden in Frost Mountain—crafted by the Dwarves who taught him... Well need to investigate this soon, but let’s rest for now.

You’ve found it. This sword... it’s more than I expected. I can feel its power, but it’s not just a weapon—it’s tied to something darker... We”ll have to travel back to the swords resting place and unveil its tainted history. Maybe those forsaken frost spiders guarding it that have plagued my lineage for centuries will give us a clue.

They’re dead, but something isn’t right. I can feel the sword changing me, just like it did my great-grandfather...The whispers are growing louder. I’m not sure how much longer I can resist... But we can’t stop now. I’ll need more from you soon...

Molten lava cascading like a waterfall... Their forges must be boiling at unimaginable heat. Now I see why dwarven craftsmanship advanced so far. No matter the effort, there are limits to how hot a fire can burn. But the land they lived in already provided perfect conditions.

Well done. This is the first time I have seen an obsidian ore of this size. The dwarves must have refined their craft by working with many different minerals since long ago. For a craftsman like me, this is like a dream come true.

Even though most of it has melted beyond recognition the condition of what remains intact is astonishing. This durability and smoothness... the dwarves are not called master craftsmen without reason. Yet I sense no unusual magic here. Then where exactly was the dagger I inherited made...
You might not have found anything legendary, but at least have these weapons for your trouble.
I know that was a lot of work, but here! Hopefully, this makes it worth your time.
I knew you wouldn’t regret it! Just look at all the valuables you brought back... and you get to keep this gift from me!

Well done, adventurer. With those beasts cleared out, my trade routes are safe again, and we can finally get back on track. I have a feeling we’re closer to uncovering the truth than ever before. Hopefully, nothing else slows us down.
Excellent work. While my wife’s health remains unchanged, the presence of family has lifted my spirits. These items should help us make progress, and I’m grateful for your dedication.
Thank you. If this turns out as I envision, it will be a weapon unlike any other. When that time comes, I shall craft one for you.
Excellent. They may not look like much, but surprisingly, fine weapons often begin with materials like these. Now I should put them to the forge and see what kind of results they produce.

Well done. Dwarven craftsmanship is impressive no matter how many times I see it. There is always something to learn from the techniques left behind by the craftsmen of old. If the opportunity arises, I should like to visit those places myself.
Such large and durable scales and talons... remarkable. Any smith would find it hard to resist a challenge like this. I am already looking forward to seeing what can be forged from them.

These weapons look like the work of dwarves. They’re the kind of craftsmen who can forge fine weapons without ever needing to rely on magic. But I suppose that wasn’t enough for them. To go even further, they must’ve reached for forbidden techniques. That hunger to make something better... I think I understand it now.

Thanks to you, things should quiet down for a while. I appreciate it. Those creatures… they’re born of malice itself. No matter how many you cut down, they just keep coming, like vermin. Until we deal with the source, this fight won’t truly be over.

By the gods, you mean they actually appeared? I can't tell if that's a blessing or a curse. Still, the fact that you brought them down is news worth hearing. Thank you for risking yourself to uncover the truth.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Weaponsmith_Extra_: Thank you for your efforts. These are quite serviceable weapons. If I examine them carefully, I am sure I will learn something from them. Now, as promised, I will give you the weapon I forged. May it serve you well.
Well done. All of this will serve as the foundation for me to make better weapons. Here, I present a new piece I recently completed. May it be of service to you, adventurer.

Well done. Thanks to you I have gained much insight and was able to complete this weapon. For now, this is the best my craft can achieve, but I will continue to strive ceaselessly to create something more perfect. For I know that effort will never betray me.

You cannot hope to forge a fine weapon by relying on luck. It takes constant practice, much experience, and even failure to shape something greater. Studying weapons already completed is of great value as well. If you bring me a few good ones, I shall exchange them for a better piece of my own making.

Forging ordinary weapons is not particularly difficult. But producing an exceptional weapon is an entirely different matter. The strength and balance a fine weapon must possess can never be fully learned by study alone. So if you bring me weapons that are a step above the last batch, I will use them as the basis to craft an even finer piece.

Adventurer, the time has come to take on a new tier. Drawing on the experience I have amassed, I intend to forge a weapon surpassing anything I have made so far. To complete it properly I require your aid. If you would procure for me several rare weapons not easily obtained, I shall present to you the fruit of my labour.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Weaponsmith_Greeti: Stone tombs, and coffins... The Forgotten Castle has an abundance of them... I bet some of them have never even been opened, but you might have to fight to be the first. What do you say?
Some fool came into the Tavern last night speaking of “Living Statues” flying around the Ruins... I haven’t ever seen such a thing, but would you mind taking a look?
I am in urgent need of Copper Ore. I am not sure how you will obtain it, but if you do, I will make it worth your while!

My great-grandfather was a master craftsman. Long ago he learned the forging techniques of the dwarves, but that knowledge led him down the wrong path. Using forbidden methods, he forged enchanted daggers and paid a heavy price. I intend to set right the mistakes of the past and forge a weapon that surpasses them through honest skill. For now, bring me a few fine weapons. Examining them will be the first step.

Let me tell you more. My great-grandfather once ventured into Frost Mountain, drawn by tales of a sword of great power. It was said to be forged by the same Dwarves who taught him their craft. If this sword is real, it could be the key to completing his legacy—and mine. Find it, and I’ll finally understand what he couldn’t.

Those spiders are not mere creatures. They are part of the curse that has followed my family for generations. My great-grandfather fought them as well and nearly lost his life in the process. If you could slay those wretched spiders, I would be able to study the sword in peace. I would be grateful for your help.

I never imagined the dwarves’ ancient homeland would lie beneath the mountain range, connected to the Goblin Caves. There was a reason we could not find even the slightest trace, no matter how thoroughly we searched Frost Mountain. At last, we can investigate the proper place. Adventurer, please confirm the dwarves’ land.

Obsidian is so rare that it is usually traded only as expensive jewelry. But weapons forged from obsidian are said to be sharper than those made from any other material. If you can bring me a small amount of obsidian, I will try forging one myself.

My great-grandfather even learned his craft from the dwarves, yet now we cannot communicate with them at all... If that is the case, conflict seems inevitable. If I cannot ask them directly, then I would like to examine the tools they have made instead. Their condition does not matter, so please bring me as many as you can.
That castle is filled with old pots, I once found a legendary Falchion inside one. Why not shatter a few and see what fortune awaits? It’s tradition around these parts.
Those pots might not have held what you’re looking for... but surely the chests scattered throughout the castle grounds will. Why don’t you open up a few and report back what you find?

If you are willing to push the limits of your safety, I can make it worth your time! I just need you to open a few Golden Chests, they are plentiful inside The Forgotten Castle. By the way, you’ll need to bring lockpicks to open those chests!

Good timing. Unfortunately, we’ll have to put our side mission on hold. A surge in monsters is wreaking havoc, and I’m almost certain it’s tied to what we were investigating. It feels like something doesn’t want us getting any closer. Even my trade routes are overrun by these beasts, so the sooner you help me clear them out, the sooner we can get back on track.

Remember that list I mentioned earlier with the glowing bug parts? There are a few more items we need to gather: some rotten fluids, high quality weapons, and ten armor scraps. It’s not a pleasant task, but I know you can handle it.

I have been racking my brain lately, trying to forge a weapon with greater power. Yet with the materials I possess, I cannot bring my idea to life. There are a few things I require, rare and not easily found. Will you help me?

I have recently been testing a new quenching method using viscous materials. The properties of metal can change greatly depending on the materials used. I hear the creatures of Firedeep yield some promising materials. I would appreciate it if you could bring me some samples.

Dwarven sites often contain clues to the craftsmanship of their builders. There is much to learn simply by studying the structures themselves or the way the stone was worked. I am curious whether any such signs remain in these newly discovered places. Take a look around and tell me what you find.

A Magma Wyvern is no ordinary wyvern. There must be a reason such a creature can survive within molten lava. If that resilience could somehow be forged into a weapon, the results might prove quite interesting. Bring me whatever materials you can obtain from the Magma Wyvern.

Adventurer, bring me a few weapons that are not easily found. My goal is to forge a blade that can pierce through anything. Though I am still far from completing such a work, I refuse to give up and continue my attempts. This time I intend to test materials that are dangerous to handle. I must study them closely and discover how they might be used.

I’ve heard rumors that new demons have begun to appear in the Inferno. They’re stronger, and they hunt adventurers with ruthless precision. It would be ideal to drive them back into the darkness before they fully settle in... but at the very least, we can’t just let them grow comfortable. Take them down. I believe if anyone can do it, it’s you.

The masters of the dungeon have grown more cunning. Those beasts have slithered into deeper shadows than ever before. Luckily, if you bring the right materials to the alchemist, he says he can craft something to draw them out. I trust his skill well enough, but I prefer certainty over guesswork. Take what he gives you, see if it truly summons those monsters, and if it does, make sure they don't walk away.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Weaponsmith_Title_: In Search of the Dwarven Land
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Woodsman_Complete_: Those supplies you gathered will keep us from being another casualty of the cold. I know this lesson all too well. There was a time, not long ago, when I lost some of my closest companions to the freezing winter. I wanted to bury them, to give them the peace they deserved, but the earth was locked in ice, cold as death itself. When I finally returned to bury them properly, their bodies had vanished.

Nice job. The path is clearer now, and those less prepared have a better shot at staying alive. It won’t be easy, but you’ve given them a damn good chance. I appreciate the help—stay sharp; we’ve still got a long way to go.

Well, I’ll be damned. She was right... I don’t know how, but it seems we’re on the right path. It’s a sliver of hope, but it’s enough for now. And between you and me, that fortune teller lady freaks me out—she eats bloody eyeballs and all sorts of strange things.

Well done. This should keep things under control for a while. But since we still don't know the source of those creatures, all we can do is clear them out from time to time. I’ll be counting on you again when the time comes.
You found some good usable pieces. Wood is heavy, so it is hard for me to carry much on my own. Thanks to you, my work will be much easier. Thank you.
Ew, that place sounds just as disgusting as I’d imagine. I’d suggest you take a bath to get some of that stench off you.
Your skills are impressive as always. Unfortunately your report seems to indicate that darkness has overtaken the castle.
I was a fool for ever doubting your skills. Here, take these items as a token of my apology.
By the gods! You’ve done it. I haven’t felt this calm in years. Unfortunately, I’m not sure how long this will last.
Ah, nothing more comforting than a crackling campfire amidst the chill of the frost.
Impressive! Those giants are renown for their strength and you made it look easy!
You've done good work here, but always remember—the mountain never rests.
A frost wyvern?! My dear, what could have compelled the demons to capture such a terrifying beast?
A fine job in thinning out the forces of evil.
Good job. I know that taking out those beasts were no easy task. I only hope we put a dent in the plans of the frost demons.

You truly heard nothing? Truly...? That can't be... Another lead, ending in nothing... Sometimes, it feels suffocating, unbearable. When I think of her, suffering even at this very moment... Haa... Haa... No, this won’t do. I need to rest. Please, leave me be for now.

Thank you. Traveling through the area has become much easier—at least for now. I hope to find what I’m looking for before those creatures swarm back again... Ah, it’s a book. According to the Alchemist, these books could aid his research. Wish me luck.
Thank you so much. I won’t forget your help. Now, I just need to bring this to the Alchemist, and I’ll receive a new potion. The effects? ...I’ll tell you about them later.
DC.Text_DesignData_Quest_Woodsman_Greeting_: People think it’s the beasts that get you in this land, but it’s not. It’s the cold. The hunger. It gets into your skin, your bones, and slowly, you’re dead before you even know it. I’ve seen too many inexperienced fools wander into the wilderness, too proud to listen to warnings, and they end up like the others. No one dies in their sleep out here unless they’re already dead. If you’re not careful, hunger and frost will do their work long before the claws of any creature ever get the chance. So it’s important to always cover your basics before any adventure.

A lot of people are helping in the search for the Leathersmith's lost daughter, but not all of them are as capable as you. There’s plenty of inexperienced souls stumbling into the wilderness, thinking they can handle it. It’s up to us to clear the path and make it safer for those who don't have the skills. We don’t want them getting in the way or becoming another burden.

Glad to see you made it back in one piece. The search for the Leathersmith’s daughter has turned up nothing, but I’ve been digging around... got desperate enough to visit that damn fortune teller. She gave me a place to check—let's see if there's any truth to her cryptic ramblings.
